purpose: Prototype exact cardinality/rank-polynomial evaluation on small smooth deterministic decomposable circuits before relying on an external TDD implementation.
semiring: N[z]/(z^(n+1)); positive literal contributes z, negative literal contributes 1, deterministic smooth OR adds coefficient vectors, decomposable AND convolves them.
circuits: two independent positive clauses: (x0 or x1) and (x2 or x3), represented with deterministic smoothed ORs
exactly one of x0,x1,x2, conjoined with a free x3 tautology
a 4-variable path-vertex-cover formula (x0 or x1)(x1 or x2)(x2 or x3) compiled first to a reduced ordered decision DAG and then evaluated as a TDD-like deterministic decision circuit
predeclared_checks: For hand-built circuits, validate decomposability of every AND and equal variable scope of every OR.
For every circuit, compare polynomial coefficients to exhaustive assignment counts by Hamming weight.
For the path formula, additionally compare to the existing exact ROBDD rank vector under at least natural and reverse variable order and require equality.
Memoization is by immutable circuit node; report node count and coefficient-operation count separately from truth-enumeration validation cost.
No result is attributed to TiDiDi/TDD authors; this is an independent local prototype of the algebraic rank-count idea.
scope: Small deterministic/smooth/decomposable circuits only. This does not establish efficiency on arbitrary TDDs or a general complexity advantage over ROBDD rank counting.
